title: Cohomology of curves
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a separated scheme of finite type
over $k$ with $\dim C\leq1$, and let $F$ be a classical torsion abelian sheaf
on $C_{\mathrm{proét}}$. With cohomology taken on $C_{\mathrm{proét}}$, the
following assertions hold:

- $(C_1)$ $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>2$.
- $(C_2)$ If $C$ is affine, $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>1$.
- $(C_3)$ If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $F$ is $p$-primary,
  $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>1$.
- $(C_4)$ If $F$ is constructible with finite stalks and prime to
  $\operatorname{char}k$, all $H^q(C,F)$ are finite.
- $(C_5)$ If $C$ is proper and $F$ is constructible with finite stalks, all
  $H^q(C,F)$ are finite.
- $(C_6)$ If $k'/k$ is an extension of algebraically closed fields and $F$ is
  prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, the pullback maps
  $H^q(C,F)\to H^q(C_{k'},F|)$ are isomorphisms.
- $(C_7)$ If $C$ is proper, the maps in $(C_6)$ are isomorphisms for every
  torsion $F$.
- $(C_8)$ For any open $U\subseteq C$, restriction
  $H^2(C,F)\to H^2(U,F|_U)$ is surjective.

In characteristic zero, the condition that $F$ be prime to the characteristic
in $(C_4)$ and $(C_6)$ is automatic.

proof.text:
This is [sk-thm-curve-package], proved in [sec-curve-estimates]. For a smooth
proper connected curve and $n$ invertible in $k$, the Kummer sequence and the
Jacobian ([sec-picard-framework]) compute $H^q(C,\mu_n)$. For $p$-primary
coefficients one uses the Artin–Schreier sequence instead. The case of general
torsion sheaves is reduced to these cases by normalization, removal of finitely
many points and a finite étale cover of degree prime to the torsion order.
